Forty-five years later, the building is Webster Hall again, and John Lydon, first known to the world as Johnny Rotten, came back to it. This time, Krasner wrote, nobody asked for their money back.
## The Lineup

The show was sold out. Lydon is still the only original member of PiL, the band he formed after the Sex Pistols fell apart. With him on stage were Lu Edmonds on guitar, Scott Firth on bass and Mark Roberts on drums, according to the review. The California punk band Plague Vendor opened with what Krasner called a high-energy set.
## The Set

The band went back to Metal Box, the 1979 record that remains PiL's defining statement, for "Poptones" and "Death Disco." They played "This Is Not a Love Song" and "Open Up," Lydon's 1993 collaboration with the electronic group Leftfield. The main set ended with a medley of "Rise" and "Religion," the crowd chanting along, Krasner reported.

Lydon sang from a music stand holding his lyrics. He danced a little, which the reviewer called the only surprising thing he did all night. Before the encore, he asked the audience politely whether they minded a three-minute break. At one point he blew his nose into a handkerchief and threw it into the crowd, a moment Krasner singled out in the review.
## The Verdict
The reviewer was not fully won over.
> "The music... tended to all sound the same after awhile." — Bob Krasner, The Villager

He allowed that it was well played. Fans' reactions online ranged from awesome to glorious, according to the review, while at least one wrote that they would not have minded a riot. Some fans paid $80 for hoodies at the merchandise table.

The room that once ended a PiL show in a riot held a calm one this time. The singer who came up in 1970s punk now reads his lyrics from a stand and asks the audience before taking a break. The songs from Metal Box were still in the set.

l7-brings-last-hurrah-farewell-tour-to-k.title: L7 Brings 'Last Hurrah' Farewell Tour to Knockdown Center Oct. 24
l7-brings-last-hurrah-farewell-tour-to-k.dek: The Los Angeles rock band plays Maspeth on the first leg of what it has called its farewell world tour.
body: L7 plays Knockdown Center in Maspeth, Queens, on Saturday, Oct. 24, on The Last Hurrah Tour, according to an event listing on The Best Parties.
The listing says the show runs from 6 p.m. to 10 p.m. at the venue, 52-19 Flushing Avenue. Tickets start at $51, sold through DICE. The page lists no opening acts and no age policy.
BrooklynVegan reported in May that the tour is the first leg of the band's farewell world tour. L7 formed in 1985, was active until 2001 and came back together in 2015, according to that report.

The fall North American run started in Phoenix on Oct. 9, BrooklynVegan reported. After New York, the band is scheduled to play Boston on Oct. 26 and Detroit on Oct. 31. The leg ends in Los Angeles on Nov. 14.

helado-negro-and-reyna-tropical-bring-he.title: Helado Negro and Reyna Tropical Bring Helado Tropical to Knockdown Center
helado-negro-and-reyna-tropical-bring-he.dek: The new duo plays Maspeth on Sunday, Oct. 25, with Nick Hakim also on the bill.
body: Helado Negro and Reyna Tropical play together as Helado Tropical at Knockdown Center in Maspeth, Queens, on Sunday, Oct. 25, according to an event listing on The Best Parties.
The listing says the show runs from 6 p.m. to 10 p.m. at 52-19 Flushing Avenue, with Nick Hakim also on the bill and other acts not yet named. Tickets start at $38. No age policy is listed.

Helado Negro is the stage name of producer and singer-songwriter Roberto Carlos Lange. Reyna Tropical is the project of guitarist and songwriter Fabi Reyna, The World from PRX reported in August. The two met in 2024 and later formed the duo. Their debut album shares the band's name and is sung in Spanish, according to that report.
The duo's U.S. tour started in San Diego on Aug. 12 and is set to end in Mexico City in November, The World reported.

brooklyn-conservatory-of-music-opens-sec.title: Brooklyn Conservatory of Music Opens Second Campus in Park Slope
brooklyn-conservatory-of-music-opens-sec.dek: The $17 million BKCM Prospect Park West building will double the conservatory's capacity for music therapy and education, according to NY1.
body: The Brooklyn Conservatory of Music has officially opened a second campus in Park Slope, NY1 reported.

The new building, called BKCM Prospect Park West, covers about 12,000 square feet and cost about $17 million to finish, the outlet reported. It holds a concert hall, a community space and music studios.

The expansion will double the conservatory's capacity for music therapy and music education, according to the report. The new building is a few blocks from the conservatory's existing space, which has served the community for 129 years.
Adam Johnston, the conservatory's deputy executive director, talked about the expansion in an interview on NY1's weekend morning program, the outlet said.
NY1 did not report how the project was paid for or describe the programs that will be offered at the new site.

natalie-maines-mocks-trump-at-beacon-the.title: Natalie Maines Criticizes Trump at Beacon Theatre Show; White House Responds
natalie-maines-mocks-trump-at-beacon-the.dek: The Chicks singer contrasted President Trump with George W. Bush during an Oct. 12 concert, and a White House spokesman answered with a statement.
body: Natalie Maines of the Chicks criticized President Trump during the band's Oct. 12 concert at the Beacon Theatre on Manhattan's Upper West Side, and the White House answered with a statement attacking the singer, Hoodline reported.

During the show, Maines said she would now give former President George W. Bush a kiss and that she was ashamed of the current president, a reversal of her 2003 remark about Bush, according to the report. She also said she would never bow to critics who tell artists to stay out of politics. MassLive reported that the show included a montage about the backlash the band faced in 2003.

On Oct. 15, White House spokesman Davis Ingle issued a statement calling Maines a "despicable nobody" and accusing her of suffering from "Trump Derangement Syndrome," according to US Weekly, as cited by Hoodline. Ingle issued a similar statement in May after Maines criticized Trump on Instagram, Taste of Country reported.

In March 2003, days before the U.S. invasion of Iraq, Maines told a London audience the band was ashamed President Bush was from Texas. Radio bans and public protests against the group followed, TIME and MassLive reported.

The Beacon show was part of the Chicks' 20-date tour marking the 20th anniversary of Taking the Long Way, which won five Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year. The tour began Sept. 30 in Detroit. An expanded reissue of the album came out Oct. 2.

arturo-ofarrill-brings-afro-latin-jazz-t.title: Arturo O'Farrill Builds an East Harlem Home for Afro Latin Jazz
arturo-ofarrill-brings-afro-latin-jazz-t.dek: The Grammy-winning bandleader's nonprofit, Belongó, is raising money to finish Casa Belongó, a performance and education center under construction in East Harlem, according to NY1.
body: Grammy-winning pianist, composer and bandleader Arturo O'Farrill is helping build a permanent home for Afro Latin jazz in East Harlem, called Casa Belongó, NY1 reported.

O'Farrill spoke with NY1 before the annual benefit for his nonprofit, Belongó, which was held the Wednesday after the Oct. 12 interview. His Afro Latin Jazz Orchestra has also started a new weekly engagement in Times Square, the outlet reported.

According to a September press release from the organization, the benefit was set for Oct. 14 at City Winery on 11th Avenue in Manhattan, with proceeds going to free music education in city public schools, community programs, free concerts and the completion of Casa Belongó. The center is under construction on Park Avenue at 118th Street. It was designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro and sits within the Timbale Terrace affordable housing development.

The program in the release included the premiere of a new O'Farrill composition that joins the blues standard House of the Rising Sun with Afro-Cuban son, and performances by Blues Brothers members Lou Marini and Leon Pendarvis, singer Daymé Arocena and the nonprofit's youth ensemble, the Fat Cats. Ballet Hispánico artistic director Eduardo Vilaro was named to receive the event's arts honor. Individual tickets started at $1,500.
O'Farrill founded Belongó in 2007 to perform, teach and preserve music of the Americas rooted in African and Indigenous traditions, according to the release.

shuttered-cobble-hill-firehouse-to-becom.title: Shuttered Cobble Hill Firehouse to Become $17.8M Music Center
shuttered-cobble-hill-firehouse-to-becom.dek: Work has begun on turning the former Engine 204 firehouse, closed since 2003, into a permanent home for the Noel Pointer Foundation's free music programs.
body: City officials broke ground Tuesday on converting the former Engine Company 204 firehouse at 299 Degraw Street in Cobble Hill into a permanent home for the Noel Pointer Foundation, a nonprofit that offers free music education, Hoodline reported. The project budget is $17.8 million.

The firehouse closed in 2003 during budget cuts under Mayor Michael Bloomberg and stood empty for years, according to Hoodline, citing PIX11 and DNAinfo. A 2007 plan to move the Brooklyn Philharmonic's offices there fell through when the orchestra faced insolvency.

City funding began in 2019 with an initial $6.5 million, and the mayor's office, City Council and Brooklyn Borough President's office now support the project, Hoodline reported. In July, the Department of Design and Construction awarded a $10.3 million contract to APN Construction Corp. of Woodside. Plans for the 6,000-square-foot building include soundproofed classrooms, recording studios, a performance hall and a garden.

The foundation, started in 1995 by Chinita Pointer in memory of her late husband, jazz violinist Noel Pointer, serves about 2,000 students a year, according to Hoodline. The new space will add piano, guitar, voice, DJing and composition to its string programs.
Construction is expected to take about two years, according to PIX11, as cited by Hoodline.

westside-cowboy-plays-music-hall-of-will.title: Westside Cowboy Plays Music Hall of Williamsburg
westside-cowboy-plays-music-hall-of-will.dek: The Manchester indie rock band's Oct. 6 Brooklyn date opened a short run of U.S. headline shows after the release of its debut album, according to The Needle Drop.
body: Westside Cowboy, an indie rock band from Manchester, England, was scheduled to headline Music Hall of Williamsburg in Brooklyn on Tuesday, Oct. 6, The Needle Drop reported.

It was the first of three U.S. dates announced in September, followed by The Foundry in Philadelphia on Oct. 10 and The Atlantis in Washington on Oct. 12, the outlet reported. They were the band's first American shows since its debut album, It Goes On, came out on Island Records in August.

The band played small shows in Los Angeles and New York in December 2025, drawing on its earlier EPs, according to the report. Several dates on its UK and European tour have sold out, The Needle Drop said.
Tickets for the U.S. shows went on sale Sept. 11. The announcement did not list prices or age restrictions for the Brooklyn date.
